newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat unchanged but well supported by bids.
newsitem.headline: French wheat unchanged but well supported by bids.

text.p: Demand at French ports for wheat remained buoyant on Monday amid further covering by exporters who as a group remain short of export licences, dealers said.

Algeria's new tender for 75,000 tonnes of April-May wheat from France, Argentina or the United States also boosted sentiment -- but traders were divided on whether French exporters would take a risk on the deal.
Rouen-delivered wheat for March continued firm at Friday's 880 francs per tonne excluding carrying charges. These are 54.53 francs for first-half March and 58.17 for second-half March.
But the market was unusually active for a Monday, a sign, some traders said, of a hectic week to come.
"The market is firm and well bid," said one trader.
Stockholders were showing little enthusiasm for selling.
Traders said France ought to be well placed to meet Algeria's request for three cargoes of wheat to be shipped between April 15 and May 31.
Slack U.S. availabilities and logistical problems in Argentina should put France out in front, they said.

But while one or two firms were said to be long, several traders warned that many exporters would be unwilling to deepen a short position for EU wheat, estimated to be up to one million tonnes for the trade as a whole.
April Rouen wheat was bid at 875 francs and May-June at 870 francs, dealers said.
March barley was stable at 855 francs for Rouen delivery.
Buyers were less visible than in wheat.
Maize, on a downtrend but propped up by wheat, was unchanged at around 860 francs delivered to Atlantic ports.
Towards the close, Matif fob barge wheat futures were up one franc a tonne for new crop on light volume of eight lots each in both September and November.
Futures for delivery nearly a year from now in February 1998 added nine francs on volume of five lots.
All French cash prices exclude carrying charges.
